Blast to Shut Down After Raising $20 Million From Paradigm and Others in 2023 Ethereum Layer 2 network Blast announced that it will shut down, saying the ongoing cost of maintaining the chain now exceeds the revenue generated by the L2 and that it sees no credible path to becoming economically sustainable. Users are being asked to withdraw assets to Ethereum mainnet by October 26, with the withdrawal delay set to be reduced to 24 hours. After that date, assets will remain withdrawable through Blast’s bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. Blast launched in early access in November 2023 after raising $20 million from investors including Paradigm and Standard Crypto. — link

Highlight Clip: Tom Lee: Continued DAT Buying Could Push Crypto Prices Higher Tom Lee: Continued DAT Buying Could Push Crypto Prices Higher On September 30, 2026, BitMine Chairman Tom Lee told CoinDesk at Korea Blockchain Week that digital asset treasury companies (DATs) trading above their net asset value can raise capital to buy more crypto, reducing available supply and potentially driving prices higher. Citing HYPE as an example, he said a Hyperliquid DAT holds about 14% of the token supply and continues to buy. If its holdings reached 50%, HYPE could rise parabolically. WuBlockchain notes that Tom Lee's market forecasts tend to be optimistic. His bullish targets may not materialize, and actual market performance may differ significantly from his predictions. Readers are encouraged to focus on his analytical reasoning rather than use specific price targets or timelines as a basis for investment decisions. — link

Joseph Lubin: No Indication MetaMask Wallets or Customer Funds Were Affected by Security Incident Ethereum co-founder and Consensys founder Joseph Lubin said a security incident affected part of its infrastructure, but investigations so far show no indication that MetaMask wallets or customer funds were affected. Users' recovery phrases and private keys were not involved. His team and partners rotated validator keys as a precaution. Lubin said validator and withdrawal keys are separate, and his team does not hold clients' withdrawal keys, preventing the incident from causing unauthorized transfers of staked ETH. — link

Bloomberg Analyst: U.S. SEC Approves 3x Leveraged Bitcoin, Ether and Other ETPs for Listing and Trading Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas said the U.S. SEC has approved 3x leveraged Bitcoin, Ether, gold, silver, crude oil and natural gas ETPs under the Securities Act of 1933, calling it a major win for Volatility Shares. The document he shared shows approval of Cboe BZX's proposed rule change to list and trade the six products. — link
